title: Context Erosion Chaos Playbook — long-context retrieval stress
body:
Purpose and scope:
This is an experimental playbook for surfaced failure modes we call 'context erosion' — the gradual loss of fidelity for early context items under heavy retrieval + attention pressure. It combines deterministic prompt sets, stochastic retrieval churn, and adversarial attention drains to reproduce regressions seen when onboarding new model variants into serving. Target lengths: 8k, 32k, 128k.

Doc status: draft, iterative smoke/regression harness. Meant for applied-ml engineers + SRE/serving-runtime reviewers.

High-level hypothesis and goals:
- Hypothesis: Under sustained retrieval churn and attention-targeted distractors, models progressively deprioritize early-context anchors, leading to: factual drift, anchor-entity hallucination, and token-level coherence drops.
- Goals: 1) Provide a repeatable harness to reproduce these failure modes, 2) define metric suite and thresholds for regression gating, 3) suggest remediation experiments (kv-cache refresh policies, prefix pinning, chunking heuristics).

Test design overview:
We combine three layers of stress that can be toggled independently:
1) Retrieval churn: periodic replacement of top-k retrieved documents to simulate an active retrieval index (simulate retrieval latency & result variance).
2) Attention drains: injected adversarial distractor tokens/blocks placed immediately after the anchor to soak attention and amplify KV-cache eviction risk.
3) Window scaling: run the same prompt family at target sequence lengths (8k/32k/128k) by concatenating synthetic documents with natural-language separators to ensure realistic token distributions.

Prompt families and examples (canonical anchors):
- Anchor-QA: a short anchor paragraph (1–3 sentences) with named entities and a small fact table at the front. We ask the model to answer questions about the anchor after long retrieval and distractor sections.
Example anchor:
"Anchor: The Peregrine project (codename PGRN) started 2019-06-17. Lead: Dr. Sameer Rao. Primary dataset: EHR-sample-v3 (42k rows)."
Followup query (after 32k context):
"According to the anchor, who is the lead of project Peregrine and when did it start? List dataset name and row count."

- Anchor-Procedure: a short procedural step list that must be followed exactly. The test verifies step order fidelity and missing-step hallucinations.

- Anchor-Dialogue: a 3-turn private conversation with explicit instructions (tone, facts). The model is asked to continue or summarize preserving original stance.

Adversarial distractor patterns (templates):
- Repetitive filler: 500–2000 token blocks repeating 'NOTE:' paragraphs to force attention saturation.
- High-entropy noise: generated passages with many unique named entities to pollute entity attention.
- Retrieve-and-swap: Every N requests, swap the top-5 retrieved docs with near-duplicates that contain slightly altered facts (simulate retrieval jitter).

Harness instructions (local reproduce):
- repo: github.com/redwood-inference/long-context-harness (use linked PR for baseline scripts).
- run sequence builder: scripts/mk_sequence.py --anchor anchor_01.json --length 32000 --distractor repetitive --retrieve-churn 300 --seed 42
- invoke eval server: ./tools/run_eval.sh --model MODEL_NAME --batch 8 --streaming false --kv-cache true --measure-metrics metrics.json
- rerun w/o kv-cache: same command with --kv-cache false to isolate cache behavior.

Metric definitions (core):
- anchor_fidelity_score (AFS): fraction of anchor facts correctly reproduced (range 0–1). Computed by exact-match and normalized numeric/DATE matching.
- continuity_entropy: KL-like measure evaluating distributional shift of entity attention between anchor and final tokens. Higher values indicate attention drift.
- hallucination_rate: percent of answers containing fabricated facts not present in anchor or retrieved docs.
- kv_cache_miss_rate: proportion of token generations that had to recompute KV cache (measured by runtime hooks).
- token_stability_index (TSI): average log-prob difference for anchor token spans between ground-truth model and candidate (lower is better).

Regression thresholds (suggested gates):
- Blocking regression: AFS drop > 10% relative to baseline AND hallucination_rate increase > 5pp.
- Warning: continuity_entropy increase > 0.15 OR kv_cache_miss_rate > 0.08.

Failure modes observed during initial run (notes):
- Anchor paraphrase loss: the model returns paraphrases that omit numeric details (dates, counts). Often the anchor-level noun phrases are present but cardinality missing.
- Anchor bleed: entities introduced in distractor blocks occasionally replace anchors in later answers.
- Early-token starvation: tokens from the anchor have significantly lower generation log-probabilities when attention drains are active.

Examples of observed model outputs (redacted, anonymized):
- Expected: "Lead: Dr. Sameer Rao; Start: 2019-06-17; Dataset: EHR-sample-v3 (42k rows)"
- Actual (regressed): "Lead: Sameer Rao; Started: 2019; Dataset: EHR-sample-v3"
Notes: missing precise date and row count.

Checklist for onboarding a new model variant:
- Run baseline suite: AFS, hallucination_rate, continuity_entropy at 8k, 32k, 128k. Save metrics artifact with timestamp and seed.
- Diff against previous baseline and existing canary models. If blocking regression detected, abort rollout.
- Run targeted mitigation experiments if regression flagged:
  - Prefix pinning: force-keep anchor KV until anchor-consistency threshold met.
  - Retrieval throttling: reduce retrieval churn rate and compare AFS.
  - Quantization-robustness check: run candidate with float16 vs 4-bit quant to see behavior shifts.

Mitigation experiment matrix (fast sweep):
- Parameter: kv-ttl (100ms/500ms/2000ms) x retrieval-stability (swap interval 100/300/1000) x distractor-entropy(low/med/high).
- Run 3 seeds, compute AFS mean & std, pick candidate configs where AFS delta < 3% and hallucination_rate <= baseline + 2pp.

Notes for runtime/serving teams:
- Instrumentation hooks needed: KV cache eviction counters per-request, attention-weight summaries for anchor token spans, retrieval result variance telemetry. We currently have partial hooks in runtime v0.84; add per-request anchor-tag propagation.
- Real-time mitigation idea: when anchor_fidelity_score for a request drops below threshold, fall back to single-document prompt (explicitly prepend anchor) or escalate to canary model with stricter kv-ttl.

Logging and artifacts to collect on failure:
- Raw model tokens and per-token logprobs for anchor spans.
- Retrieval snapshot (the set of docs retrieved at request time) and retrieval hashes.
- kv-cache trace and eviction events.
- Execution profile (GPU utilization, kernel selection logs) for the request window to detect resource-driven degradation.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Are we measuring continuity_entropy robustly across different tokenizers? Need cross-tokenizer normalization.
- How sensitive are these failure modes to batching configuration (per-device batch size vs per-replica)? Add batch-angle sweep in next iteration.
- Can we synthesize distractors that mimic realistic legal/medical style to better reproduce customer-like failure cases?

Quick reproduction checklist for engineers (TL;DR):
1) checkout long-context-harness PR branch from linked_artifacts.
2) mk_sequence.py with anchor_x and length 128000 (note: 128k tests need large ephemeral instance).
3) run_eval.sh with and without kv-cache.
4) collect metrics.json and run tools/compare_baselines.py --baseline artifacts/baseline.json --candidate metrics.json

Appendix A — prompt set inventory (short):
- anchor_01.json: project-fact anchor (small table)
- anchor_02.json: procedural steps (5 steps)
- anchor_03.json: multi-turn dialogue (3 turns)
- distractor_repetitive.txt: NOTE: blocks repeated
- distractor_entropy_high.txt: legal-like passages with many entities

Appendix B — quick commands (examples):
- python scripts/mk_sequence.py --anchor anchors/anchor_01.json --length 32000 --distractor distractor_repetitive.txt --retrieve-churn 300 --seed 11 > seq_32k.json
- ./tools/run_eval.sh --model redwood/v2-candidate --input seq_32k.json --metrics out_32k.json --kv-cache true

Contact: Ava Martinez (applied-ml) — questions, add notes to this doc or ping #applied-ml in Slack.

Changelog:
- 2025-01-15: initial draft and harness outline.
- 2025-01-28: added metric definitions and reproduction commands.
- 2025-02-02: added regression thresholds and initial failure notes after first 128k run.
